name: Victoria Spartz
signature: Indiana Republican who broke with state boosters to demand a federal review of the LEAP district and data center buildout over who pays for power and water; longtime antitrust reformer aimed at Big Tech.

notable_quote.text: We cannot retire firm generation, add massive new loads, spend hundreds of millions on infrastructure, and then leave Hoosiers guessing who will pay for it

data_centers.summary: Spartz wants data centers built only if Hoosiers are protected from higher electric bills, water strain and blackout risk. In September 2026 she asked the Energy and Interior secretaries for an independent federal review of the LEAP district and the Meta, Google and Amazon projects, while saying she still supports bringing strategic industries to Indiana.

evidence.title: Press release: Spartz seeks independent federal review of Indiana data centers and LEAP (letter to Energy Sec. Wright and Interior Sec. Burgum)
evidence.quote: I support bringing advanced manufacturing and strategic industries to Indiana, but Hoosier families, farmers, small businesses, and existing industries should not be forced to subsidize extraordinary private projects.
evidence.what_it_shows: She asks for a full federal accounting of energy, water, grid costs and who pays before Indiana commits to the LEAP and hyperscale projects.

evidence.title: Press release: Spartz says she has raised data center energy and LEAP water concerns for two years
evidence.quote: For two years, I have been raising concerns about the massive energy and infrastructure demands of data centers, as well as the significant water demands of the LEAP district
evidence.what_it_shows: She frames grid load, transmission costs and the 25 million gallon per day White River water plan as ratepayer and reliability problems.

evidence.title: IndyStar: Spartz says LEAP district lacks transparency, calls for federal review (quotes her letter)
evidence.quote: Hoosier families, farmers, small businesses, and existing industries should not subsidize extraordinary private projects through higher utility bills, taxpayer-funded infrastructure, or reduced reliability
evidence.what_it_shows: Her letter blames Indiana laws for closed-door LEAP deals and asks for ratepayer protections against stranded costs.

evidence.title: LarryInFishers: Ford challenges Spartz on data centers after her call for federal review
evidence.quote: Spartz said she supports advanced manufacturing and strategic industries coming to Indiana, but existing residents and businesses should not subsidize extraordinary private projects.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her Democratic opponent calls the review request election-year posturing and urges her to file federal legislation giving communities control and barring cost shifts to ratepayers.

ai_risk.summary: Spartz has not spoken publicly about AI safety rules. Her one AI-specific act is signing a March 2026 letter praising the Energy Department's Genesis Mission to deploy AI in science and keep America ahead of China, which leans pro-innovation.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter: Lawmakers laud Trump administration's AI Genesis Mission (Spartz co-signed the Gooden letter to Energy Sec. Wright)
evidence.quote: Private sector innovators play a critical role in ensuring the United States remains the global leader in emerging technologies.
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a letter celebrating rapid AI deployment through public-private partnerships, with no mention of safety rules.

tech_regulation.summary: Spartz is a populist on Big Tech: she co-led bipartisan antitrust reform bills in 2021 and 2022 citing abuses by Big Tech, cosponsored the TikTok divest-or-ban law, and in 2026 cosponsored the Flock-Off Act to defund AI-assisted license plate surveillance cameras.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Spartz urges colleagues to support bipartisan, bicameral antitrust reform package
evidence.quote: I am glad to co-lead this bicameral antitrust reform effort to deal with abusive monopoly powers, including infringements on our Constitutional rights by Big Tech.
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed stronger merger fees, state antitrust enforcement venue rules and foreign subsidy disclosure, naming Big Tech as a target.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Spartz co-leads bipartisan bill to address Big Tech and other monopoly powers (Merger Filing Fee Modernization Act)
evidence.quote: Competition and free markets are fundamental to our freedoms. Ever-increasing government regulations have created distortions and contributed to a rise in monopolies and oligopolies in many sectors of our economy
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants more antitrust enforcement resources but frames the problem partly as government-created distortions.

evidence.title: Press release (Massie): Reps. Massie, Burlison introduce the Flock-Off Act to defund surveillance state cameras; Spartz is an original cosponsor
evidence.quote: Original cosponsors of the Flock-Off Act include Rep. Lauren Boebert (R-CO), Rep. Paul Gosar (R-AZ), Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA), Rep. Chip Roy (R-TX), and Rep. Victoria Spartz (R-IN).
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a cross-party bill to cut federal funds for automated license plate readers and biometric surveillance cameras.

evidence.title: H.R. 7521 (118th), Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok divest-or-ban)
evidence.what_it_shows: She cosponsored the law forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to sell or face a ban.

evidence.title: H.R. 4791 (118th), Free Speech Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed barring officials from pressuring platforms to remove posts, a conservative free-speech angle on tech policy.

preemption.summary: Spartz voted for the House version of the 2025 budget bill that carried a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws, but she has never spoken about preemption itself. Her opponent J.D. Ford uses that vote against her; no statement from her on the issue was found.

evidence.title: House roll call 145 (May 22, 2025): Spartz voted Yea on H.R. 1, whose House text included a 10-year moratorium on state and local AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: A vote for the whole package, not a statement on preemption; the moratorium was later stripped by the Senate.

evidence.title: LarryInFishers: Ford cites Spartz's H.R. 1 vote and its restrictions on state and local AI regulation
evidence.quote: The House clerk's record confirms Spartz voted for the bill on May 22, 2025.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her challenger argues the vote would have undermined communities' ability to regulate AI data centers; Spartz has not responded on preemption.

china_chips.summary: No public position found. Searches for Spartz with Nvidia, export controls, chips and China turned up nothing, and she has not sponsored or cosponsored chip export bills in the 118th or 119th Congress.

No AI super PAC support or attacks found (not on Leading the Future's GOP Champions list).

name: Jefferson Shreve
signature: Freshman appropriator focused on keeping advanced chips away from China (BIS STRENGTH Act sponsor, Chip Security Act cosponsor), praised in Public First Action ads; cosponsor of a bill keeping data center approvals in local hands.

notable_quote.text: Export controls only work if we have the experts to enforce them. This bill strengthens BIS with the specialized talent it needs to stay ahead of evolving threats, protect America's technological edge, and defend our national security.

groups: Stop Scams Caucus (listed on his official site)

data_centers.summary: Shreve has made no public statements about data centers. His only action is cosponsoring the Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act in September 2026, which keeps approval power with local governments. A first-pass lead that he also cosponsored grid-buildout bills could not be verified.

evidence.title: H.R. 10119, Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (Barrett)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs keeping the power to approve or block new data centers with local towns and cities rather than federal override.

ai_risk.summary: No public position found. Searches for Shreve with artificial intelligence, AI regulation, chatbots and deepfakes returned nothing on AI safety rules, and his AI-related bills all concern chip exports and China.

tech_regulation.summary: Shreve's tech record is about scams: he cosponsored the Romance Scam Prevention Act, which makes dating apps warn users about banned scammers, and his site lists a Stop Scams Caucus. No statements on Big Tech, Section 230 or kids online safety were found.

evidence.title: H.R. 2481, Romance Scam Prevention Act
evidence.what_it_shows: A targeted consumer-protection rule for dating platforms.

preemption.summary: Mixed and thin. Shreve voted for the House budget bill that carried the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws in May 2025, but Public First Action later credited him among Republicans who worked to keep federal preemption of state AI laws out of the defense bill. He has not spoken on the issue himself.

evidence.title: House roll call 145 (May 22, 2025): Shreve voted Yea on H.R. 1, whose House text included a 10-year moratorium on state and local AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: A vote for the whole package, not a statement on preemption; the moratorium was later removed.

evidence.title: H.R. 6275, China AI Power Report Act

evidence.title: H.R. 7058, Foreign Adversary AI Risk Assessment and Diplomacy Act

evidence.title: H.R. 8288, Strengthening Export Controls Compliance Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Helps small businesses comply with export rules.

evidence.title: Public First Action Conservative AI Consensus Project ads highlight Shreve's record on the Chip Security Act and export controls

name: André Carson
signature: Indianapolis Democrat who joined the Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez AI data center moratorium bill after primary pressure, wrote a data center site transparency bill, signed the letter against NDAA preemption of state AI laws, and is hawkish on chips to China.

notable_quote.text: Data centers cannot come at a cost to American families, who are already facing high grocery, gas, and housing costs

groups: Congressional Artificial Intelligence Caucus (member, per first-pass landscape research; not shown on his site's caucus list)
Monopoly Busters Caucus (member, per his official site)
Internet of Things Caucus (member, per his official site)
House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (member)

data_centers.summary: Carson wants a pause. After primary challengers attacked his silence in spring 2026, he announced support for a federal data center moratorium, co-introduced the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act, and in June 2026 joined the Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez AI Data Center Moratorium Act. He has also cosponsored bills on ratepayer costs, energy and water disclosure, federal lands and siting.

evidence.title: Press release: Carson introduces data center moratorium bill (AI Data Center Moratorium Act with Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez)
evidence.quote: We need to make sure workers, families, and neighborhoods aren't forced to pay the burden of this rapidly rising technology without guardrails. Our bill would enact a pause until we can guarantee common sense protections.
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs an immediate federal moratorium on new AI data centers until safeguards on bills, jobs and the environment exist.

evidence.title: H.R. 9442, Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Formal cosponsorship of the pause bill.

evidence.title: Press release: Carson introduces bill to stop surprise AI data center developments (AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act with McIver and Foushee)
evidence.quote: Data centers are often shrouded in mystery, with plans moving forward before meaningful public input. Our bill will change that, requiring data centers to be transparent.
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill requires 180-day public notice, disclosure of power and water use, and limits on NDAs with public bodies.

evidence.title: E&E News: Data center moratorium a fault line in Dem primaries (Carson statement after challengers cited AES Indiana donations)
evidence.quote: work to pass bills to prevent data centers from passing costs on to customers and to require environmental disclosures
evidence.what_it_shows: He shifted to supporting a federal moratorium while facing primary challengers Destiny Wells and George Hornedo.

evidence.title: Letter from 20 House Democrats led by Rep. Kevin Mullin to FERC, Edison Electric Institute and the Data Center Coalition on data center energy costs (Carson co-signed)
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked regulators and utilities how they will keep grid upgrade costs off household bills.

evidence.title: H.R. 6529, Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Keeps families' electric bills from paying for data center grid buildout.

evidence.title: H.R. 6984, Data Center Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires public reporting of data center electricity and water use.

evidence.title: H.R. 9939, No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Bans AI data centers on federal land.

evidence.title: H.R. 10321, Responsible Data Center Siting Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Sets siting rules so data centers do not overload local power and water.

ai_risk.summary: Carson backs targeted rules: bills banning AI discrimination and requiring bias audits, a ban on AI-driven price and wage discrimination, and election deepfake bans. The data center moratorium bill he joined also conditions building on national AI safety safeguards, though his own words focus on costs and jobs rather than existential risk.

evidence.title: H.R. 6356, Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Bans discriminatory AI and requires pre- and post-deployment testing.

evidence.title: H.R. 7110, Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Creates agency civil rights teams to catch unfair algorithms.

evidence.title: H.R. 4640, Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Bans using AI and personal data to set different prices or wages for different people.

evidence.title: Transcript: Carson's opening statement at Select Committee hearing on China's Campaign to Steal America's AI Edge
evidence.quote: We can enact protections for workers against displacement, ensure communities do not face hikes to their utility bills, and ensure civil rights and human rights are designed into the algorithms.
evidence.what_it_shows: He ties winning the AI race with China to writing worker, utility and civil rights protections into the rules.

evidence.title: Press release: Carson introduces data center moratorium bill (bill text pauses data centers until AI is shown safe and effective)
evidence.quote: Data centers have the potential to create good union jobs, but they also have the potential to eliminate jobs.
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill he joined makes new AI infrastructure wait for national safety, worker and environmental safeguards, a stricter stance than his own framing.

evidence.title: H.R. 5628 (118th), Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for mandatory bias and harm testing of automated systems.

evidence.title: H.R. 4894, Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Bans AI-made election lies in the run-up to federal elections.

tech_regulation.summary: Carson favors targeted rules on tech companies: he belongs to the Monopoly Busters Caucus, cosponsored the ban on AI price gouging, the TikTok divest-or-ban law, election deepfake labeling bills and a ban on algorithmic rent-setting cartels.

evidence.title: Carson official site: Caucus memberships list includes Monopoly Busters Caucus and Internet of Things Caucus
evidence.what_it_shows: He identifies with the House's anti-monopoly bloc.

evidence.title: H.R. 4640, Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: New federal rule on how companies can use personal data and algorithms in pricing.

evidence.title: H.R. 7521 (118th), Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed forcing TikTok's sale or ban.

evidence.what_it_shows: Would outlaw landlords' use of shared pricing algorithms to push up rents.

evidence.title: H.R. 7766 (118th), Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires labels and watermarks on AI-generated media.

preemption.summary: Carson opposes federal preemption of state AI laws. He signed the December 2025 Clarke letter from 44 House Democrats telling defense-bill negotiators that any AI moratorium or preemption should stay out of the NDAA, and he voted against the House budget bill that carried the 10-year state AI law moratorium.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA (Carson signed)
evidence.quote: a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined colleagues arguing preemption would create a regulatory vacuum for Big Tech and stomp on state autonomy.

evidence.title: House roll call 145 (May 22, 2025): Carson voted Nay on H.R. 1, whose House text included a 10-year moratorium on state and local AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: A party-line vote against the whole bill, consistent with but not specific to opposing preemption.

china_chips.summary: Carson wants tighter chip controls. He cosponsored the Chip Security Act and the No Advanced Chips for the CCP Act, and at an April 2026 Select Committee hearing he said Commerce should go after chip smugglers and companies like DeepSeek with everything it has, while also arguing that immigration and research cuts weaken America's lead.

evidence.title: Transcript: Carson's opening statement at Select Committee hearing on China's Campaign to Steal America's AI Edge
evidence.quote: Chinese companies like DeepSeek cannot and should not get away with stealing our most innovative tech. The Commerce Department should go after those who break laws and break the rules with everything they've got.
evidence.what_it_shows: He calls for strict enforcement of chip export laws and a coalition with the Netherlands and Japan on lithography.

evidence.title: H.R. 3447, Chip Security Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires location verification on advanced AI chips to catch diversion to China.

evidence.title: H.R. 5022, No Advanced Chips for the CCP Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Would block the most powerful chips from being sold to China.

evidence.title: H.R. 802, STAR Act of 2025 (chip factory tax credit)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports domestic chip manufacturing incentives alongside export limits.

tech_regulation.summary: Houchin is one of the House's leading kids-online-safety Republicans. She founded and co-chairs the Kids Online Safety Caucus, cosponsored KOSA and COPPA 2.0, sponsored the RESET (now GUARDIAN) Act on parental consent and the 16 & Up Social Media Act, and says Congress must hold Big Tech accountable and stop platforms hiding behind Section 230.

evidence.title: Press release: Houchin launches bipartisan Kids Online Safety Caucus
evidence.quote: Congress must hold Big Tech accountable when their platforms put children at risk.
evidence.what_it_shows: She created a caucus focused on platform transparency, parental tools and AI-driven risks to minors.

evidence.title: Joint statement from Kids Online Safety Caucus co-chairs Houchin and Auchincloss on Meta, YouTube verdict
evidence.quote: continue to hide their exploitation of children behind bad-faith Section 230 defenses
evidence.what_it_shows: She calls for a federal age assurance law setting internet adulthood at 16 with liability for apps.

preemption.summary: Houchin wants one national AI rule. She was an original supporter of the Obernolte-Trahan Great American AI Act discussion draft, which preempts state AI development laws for three years, warning against a patchwork of fifty state laws, and she cosponsored the FRONTIER Act, which sets a uniform national standard to prevent state patchwork rules. She also voted for the House budget bill carrying the 10-year state AI law moratorium.

evidence.title: Press release (Trahan): Trahan, Obernolte unveil federal AI framework discussion draft (Great American AI Act; Houchin statement)
evidence.quote: America should lead the world in artificial intelligence, not regulate ourselves into falling behind China through a patchwork of fifty different state laws
evidence.what_it_shows: She endorses a federal framework that includes a three-year preemption of state AI development laws.

evidence.title: Press release (Obernolte): Obernolte, Trahan release discussion draft of the Great American AI Act (Houchin statement)
evidence.quote: This bill creates a clear national standard for how AI models are developed while preserving the ability of states and parents to protect children.
evidence.what_it_shows: She accepts preemption of state model-development rules while carving out state child-protection laws.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Bipartisan AI draft proposes three-year preemption of state laws (Houchin among six members releasing the draft)
evidence.quote: Notably, it includes a three-year preemption of state laws related to AI development that has previously generated significant pushback for Trahan.
evidence.what_it_shows: Independent confirmation that the draft she backed preempts state AI development laws.

evidence.title: Press release (Obernolte): FRONTIER Act introduced with Houchin as original cosponsor; creates a uniform national standard
evidence.quote: It also creates a uniform national standard for transparency, auditing, and reporting of catastrophic risk to prevent a patchwork of state regulations.
evidence.what_it_shows: The frontier-AI bill she cosponsored is designed to displace state-by-state rules.

evidence.title: House roll call 145 (May 22, 2025): Houchin voted Yea on H.R. 1, whose House text included a 10-year moratorium on state and local AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: Consistent with her later support for a national standard.
